title: Texas vs California on $75,000 (2026)
source: Figures from https://dolidob.com/data/take-home-2026.json (single filer, paid every two weeks, no 401(k)).

lines.speaker: bob
lines.text: Dolly, I got two job offers. Same pay, seventy-five thousand dollars. One in Texas, one in California.

lines.speaker: dolly
lines.text: Nice! Same salary, but you won't take home the same amount.

lines.speaker: dolly
lines.text: Federal tax is the same in both: about seven thousand six hundred seventy dollars.

lines.speaker: dolly
lines.text: Social Security and Medicare are the same too: about five thousand seven hundred dollars.

lines.speaker: dolly
lines.text: The state. Texas has no income tax on wages. California takes about four thousand dollars, with state disability insurance.

lines.speaker: bob
lines.text: So how much do I keep?

lines.speaker: dolly
lines.text: In Texas, about sixty-one thousand six hundred a year. In California, about fifty-seven thousand six hundred.

lines.speaker: bob
lines.text: That's four thousand dollars a year, just for the state!

lines.speaker: dolly
lines.text: Check your own state and salary free at dolidob dot com. Estimates only, not tax advice.
